# Saved projects

Open `/saved-projects.html` from the existing Stellar Forge application. The page collects work saved in the original shared draft store and opens each supported project in its original editor. The existing grant manuscript and source publisher remain independent of the browser's saved work.

## Scope and complete originals

The desk covers merchant setup, CoCart customer setup, SCF submission drafts, recorded submission reviews and unfinished submission-review working copies. Each record keeps its original ID, revision, name, timestamp and complete input, including retained source files, field text, original export text, review notes and unresolved input supported by its original editor. Unknown record kinds remain visible and downloadable without conversion.

The shared store is `stellar-forge-merchant-drafts`, version 1, object store `drafts`. This feature uses that same database. Companion-reader and Source Desk workspaces have separate stores and remain in their own original export/receive workflows. Unsaved forms in another editor are not a saved project: use that editor's Save or complete export before leaving it.

The desk adds its own receiving history and working reviews to the same store under reserved IDs. The original merchant picker shows merchant records, while this desk separates project records, receiving history and unfinished library reviews. No incoming history becomes a local command merely because it was included in an archive.

## Find, open and back up

Search by project name, type or ID, and order by name, type or last saved time. Selection survives filters. **Download selected** includes complete selected projects, together with the desk's retained receiving history and unfinished receiving reviews. **Download complete backup** selects all project records in this shared store. Both use one complete read-only database transaction for the source snapshot.

Open a project through its original workflow link. Merchant setup, CoCart and submission links select the exact saved ID; their existing editors retain their own validation and revision guards. A recorded review opens through its existing review ID. Opening a submission-review working copy uses that workflow's existing independent-copy behavior. Unsupported record kinds have no guessed editor link.

**Inspect** shows the complete record representation, with a bounded visual preview if the record is large. Its Download action contains every field. This single-record inspection format is separate from the complete archive format used by Receive archive; use Download selected for a directly receiveable one-project archive.

The archive is JSON with an identified body and full record hashes. A tagged graph represents undefined values, exact special numbers, sparse arrays, dates, binary buffers/views, shared objects and cycles instead of silently coercing them to ordinary JSON. Binary view offsets and shared backing buffers survive receiving. Unsupported structured object types fail clearly; preserve those through their original workflow. Plain strings, including unfinished text, retain their exact JavaScript contents.

Each archive is limited to 256 MiB and 5,000 total project/history/working records. Whole records are never truncated to fit. The API can omit history or working copies explicitly for a project-only transfer; the staff desk's default backup includes both. Clear the relevant checkboxes for an explicit project-only transfer. A history/working-only backup is available even when no project records remain. The inventory remains available when the store is larger; the bound applies to the complete selected archive.

## Receive and compare

Choose the complete archive file. Its raw text is retained in a local working review before validation. A malformed or incomplete file can therefore still be downloaded or reopened for correction; it is never treated as a completed project import.

A comparison shows each incoming project against its current complete local record:

- **New:** restore the original project or keep the current absent position.
- **Identical:** keep the identical original.
- **Conflict:** keep local work or explicitly replace it. Replacement retains the complete beforeimage in the receiving history.
- **Restore new projects:** restore only absent IDs and keep existing IDs. It does not invent new IDs for opaque projects.
- **Keep all local work:** record that choice without overwriting projects.

Project IDs are preserved across independent receiving. The desk does not rewrite nested native identities to manufacture separate copies. To create an independent submission or merchant copy, use that original editor's Save as new action.

Before applying, the full comparison, choices, request ID and exact archive text are saved as one unfinished working review. All project comparisons, selected writes and the original receiving receipt then commit in a single IndexedDB read-write transaction. A changed local record aborts the transaction. Recompare explicitly and review the resulting choices; another window's edits are never silently adopted as a new baseline.

Restoring an absent project keeps its original saved record. Replacing an existing project increments the current local revision and timestamp while preserving the complete incoming input. The receipt retains both the incoming original and previous local record.

## Reloads, conflicts and uncertain responses

The URL identifies the current saved working review. Reloading restores its exact raw archive, choices and any pending original request. A pending request is frozen. **Recover original result** resends that same request ID, body and comparison. The transaction checks for its completed receipt before checking a stale baseline, so replay returns the first result even after later project edits.

A working-review save uses the original draft revision guard. If another window saved that working review first, download the complete current review or choose **Save as separate working copy**. A fork of pending work retains the same pending operation ID and original comparison; it cannot create a second receiving operation accidentally.

The completed receipt is separate from the current recipient summaries. Later edits remain visible as current state and do not change the original receipt. Downloading a working review retains its complete raw text and request. Importing that downloaded review creates a new local review: earlier requests remain passive source history and a fresh explicit comparison is required before any new application.

Closing a review saves it and removes it only from the active screen. This feature does not delete the retained review. Malformed unfinished input remains available for full download.

## History and selective undo

Open a receiving result to inspect its original decision receipt, separately observed current project summaries and passive imported history. Full downloaded results include the original archive and complete before/after records. A backup includes these receipts so an independent recipient can retain their history.

Undo is selective. Compare the receipt's accepted after-values with the current saved records. An unchanged replacement can return to its original local input as a new local revision. An unchanged project created by receiving can be removed. A project that staff changed or deleted since receiving is unavailable for undo. Unselected and staff-changed records are reported separately and remain untouched.

Undo has its own durable working request and receipt, committed atomically against the selected unchanged current records. If those records change between review and application, the operation aborts. Recover an uncertain undo using its original ID; do not create a new request merely because an acknowledgment was lost.

Incoming history is passive. It does not authorize undo against unrelated local records. A recovered incoming unfinished working review creates a new local copy retaining the exact original record as provenance. Its earlier receiving/undo request, comparison and recipient links remain passive; compare again with this browser.

## Privacy and operational limits

Archives contain the full original saved inputs and may include source exports, commercial notes, unfinished answers and earlier receiving archives. Review recipients before sharing. The desk uses local browser storage and explicit downloads; it does not send saved projects to a server.

Use HTTPS or the existing loopback host for Web Crypto and IndexedDB. Browser storage availability and quota still apply. An unavailable or full store is an error, not a saved result. Complete downloaded archives are the portable copies to retain before clearing browser data.

The archive hashes establish internal byte/value consistency, not the author's identity or permission to act on an external system. Receiving a project does not submit a grant, publish a website, make a payment, run a customer service or approve a review.

## Maintained integration

`dist/saved-project-library.mjs` owns archive interpretation, original record summaries, receiving and undo. `drafts.mjs` retains the original database owner and adds complete snapshot and atomic multi-record operations. The staff interface is `saved-projects.html/.mjs/.css`. The existing browser asset manifest exposes these complete files; `saved-projects.mjs` at the developer-site root supplies additive navigation and asset composition helpers.

The maintained package exports `./grant/saved-projects` and `./grant/saved-projects/composition`. Keep the same complete source edition together, including the shared draft store. Browser storage/receiving success requires operating the real installed page; source review and syntax parsing alone do not establish that result.

### Programmatic interface

- `readLibrary()`: project, local receipt and working-review summaries.
- `exportProjects({ids,label,includeHistory:true,includeWorking:true})`: complete text, filename, exact raw SHA/bytes and archive ID.
- `openArchive(text)`: validated serializable archive view retaining exact original text.
- `reviewReceiving(archive)`: serializable incoming/current comparison and complete expected records.
- `commitReceiving({archive,review,choices,requestId,label})`: first receipt, replay flag and separate current summaries.
- `readReceipt(id)`, `exportReceipt(id)`: original result and passive history.
- `reviewUndo(receiptId)`, `commitUndo({review,ids,requestId,label})`: selective unchanged-record recovery.
- `saveWorking({id,revision,value})`, `loadWorking(id)`: original guarded local working records.
- `recoverWorking(receiptId,sourceWorkingId)`: a new local working copy with complete value and passive original provenance.
- `downloadProject(id)`: complete single-record inspection representation.

Use explicit stable request IDs. Keep an opaque archive/review exactly as returned. Retry the same request after an uncertain result; prepare a new comparison only as an explicit subsequent operation.

SCF #46 / DEVELOPER TOOLING / OPEN TRACK

Stellar Discovery
Trust Layer

From an approved payment
to complete, useful work.

TokenJunkieLabs requests USD 38,000 equivalent in XLM for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance. The work installs a useful paid Stellar service with two independently operated merchants, two independent buyer operators and the same selected operation through two independently operated facilitators.

The product is open-source, self-hostable merchant and buyer tooling. It carries an approved API request, dataset or paid MCP tool through native settlement, complete useful output, fulfillment and operating handover. The merchant controls its source and terms. The buyer controls its keys, request and spending. Another engineer can reopen the installation and recover unfinished work.

The working development baseline comprises 18 distinct team-operated purchases totaling 411,000 stroops, or 0.0411 native testnet XLM, with network fees recorded separately. The funded milestones establish independent customer operation, repeated use and production receiving from that baseline.

    Project and requested outcome

A merchant publishes an authorized resource; a buyer approves the exact request and total spending, pays through Stellar, and receives the complete result in its application.     Why Stellar and what we contribute

    Stellar supplies authorization and settlement for the selected purchase. In the existing x402 Exact flow, the buyer signs token-transfer authorization binding payer, recipient, atomic amount and expiration. A facilitator submits it on the selected network; fee sponsorship can cover the transaction fee. We use existing Stellar SDKs and token contracts.

    Our application binds that transfer to the exact HTTP request or MCP tool/arguments, selected source, payment option, complete customer output and fulfillment history. The buyer controls wallet authority and total spend; the merchant controls source access, pricing and fulfillment.

    The ecosystem already supplies substantial infrastructure. Stellar's x402 client libraries handle payment challenges, Soroban authorization and signed retries; the Stellar CLI supplies the signing identity. Facilitators verify and settle, and Bazaar describes discoverable resources. ApiCharge's published proxy/access-grant approach provides typed paid access and retained purchased service levels. MPP Router provides paid proxy access, request-ID response caching and signed job polling. Our proposed Open Track contribution is a reusable way to keep an entire paid customer task coherent across those components: the reviewed source and query, aggregate approval, distinct native transfers, every agreed page/file, editable output, interrupted-delivery recovery, accounting and independent maintenance. The application retains the original relationship among those records when a provider, source edition or receiving operator changes. The two customer installations develop the remaining source/consumer and deployment joins and return reusable improvements to that public workflow. Open Track fit rests on this technical and customer-operation contribution and its measured usefulness; the selected track remains subject to the issuer’s invitation and review.

    The programme makes that contribution measurable. It installs two independent services and buyers, operates the same useful service through two testnet facilitators, and carries both merchants into recurring mainnet use. The two-provider comparison holds the service, schema, source population and useful output constant. Existing catalogs do not by themselves establish this compatibility: the retained Vellar/Periplo comparison found no shared seller/route identity, so explicit registration and integration of the same service is part of the funded work.

**Stellar Discovery Trust Layer — TokenJunkieLabs — SCF #46 Build / Open Track**

## Project and requested outcome

We are building open-source, self-hostable software for operating paid APIs, datasets and agent tools on Stellar. A merchant selects the resource and commercial terms; a buyer approves a specific request and controls its wallet and spending. The software carries that agreement through native settlement, complete usable output, fulfillment, recovery and handover to another engineer.

We request **USD 38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance**. The award will fund the remaining source, consumer and deployment engineering for **two independently operated merchants and two independent buyer operators**, including completion of the same useful operation through **two independently operated facilitators**. The delivered result will be a maintainable service on Stellar mainnet, with recurring customer use and an independently completed recovery and handover.

The existing product supplies the architecture, merchant and buyer workspaces, source adapters, payment integration, result receiving and operating controls. The six funded packages below apply that product to the selected customers’ actual sources, applications and hosts. They include installation-specific implementation and defects, provider integration, deployed threat response, production release and technical receiving.

## Customer problem, need and adoption

API and data operators want to sell useful operations to applications and agents while retaining source rights, access rules and commercial control. Buyers need the complete result they approved, in a form their existing application can use. Staff also need to recover an interrupted paid request and transfer the working service to another maintainer.

That task joins four records: the approved request, the settled transfer, the delivered output and the accepted fulfillment or accounting. A payment confirmation alone does not show whether a multi-page dataset is complete, whether its values retained their original meaning, or whether an order reached its intended state. The customer’s useful task can contain several priced requests, so its aggregate cost and complete output must remain visible.

Public October 2–3 x402 reports illustrate this operational need: one merchant rejected payment-bearing requests because its POST requirement differed from a client’s GET retry; another reported settlement without its expected discovery listing. These reports concerned Base deployments, and their follow-ups include a corrected server and successful indexing. They inform the request, discovery and recovery joins we implement on Stellar.

Our current human conversations provide more specific customer learning:

|Organization|Observed response|Proposed useful implementation|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|Veridex|Invited an open testnet design partnership after declining a third-party testing budget.|One agreed testnet route and buyer adaptation, proposed at $1,500 over five business days.|
|Nansen|Referred the proposal internally and confirmed on October 12 that the Holdings detail was included.|Read-only Ethereum Holdings data, Stellar testnet payment and source/operator handover, proposed at $2,400 over five business days.|
|CoCart|Founder Sébastien Dumont asked about introductions, the payer, referral compensation, responsibilities and contracting.|One customer’s headless cart, native WooCommerce checkout, payment/order operation and receiving, proposed at $7,200 for 60 hours over fifteen business days.|
|Blockscout|Mojmir Racak expressed interest on October 12 and reported no current integration budget.|One approved PRO API token-information operation, buyer integration and handover, proposed at $4,800 over ten business days.|


These conversations identify the practical selection decisions: a recurring buyer task, usable source rights, an accountable merchant host, an independent receiving application and an agreed commissioning payer. A participating platform and the organization paying for its integration can be different organizations. For CoCart, the first merchant or agency and commissioning arrangement remain to be selected. Bryce owns these favorable relationships and subsequent agreements.

For each funded installation, the original workorder will name the payer, merchant, buyer and receiving operator; the source and authorized access; the exact request, complete output and priced unit; the host and receiving application; and the person accepting delivery. It will record what makes a later purchase useful, such as a fresh period, changed source edition or new customer request. The implementation team then takes that same task through deployment, complete result receiving, recurring use and maintainer handover.

**Environmental provider intake supplies a concrete commissioning path.** Axiom Data Science's [published sensor-intake guidance](https://www.axiomdatascience.com/best-practices/SubmitDataSensors.html) describes delays caused by inconsistent provider fields and asks for station, time, quality, contact and licensing context. Our proposed workshare applies the complete ERDDAP provider workspace to three agreed feeds, one client-managed Linux installation and one file/command receiving integration: **$12,600 / 96 hours / 18 active business days**, including eight support hours during the first 30 days after acceptance. The first contact and four customer documents were sent on October 12; commissioning remains open. The original public-source operation has received a complete 144-row NDBC dataset and saved three provider-review revisions, with earlier exports preserved through an evaluator upgrade. Its selected installation and browser continuation remain pending. If selected for funded deployment, the parties would agree the merchant, independent buyer, exact useful output and payment terms in the original workorder. §9A connects this task to the existing six funded packages. [Current product and operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/5f7143f88bb28fbd0c1b63a913545633c475afd6/products/erddap-provider/OPERATING.md) · [Original commercial delivery](https://tokenjunkielabs.slack.com/archives/C0BTTA66TK3/p1791809627823129?thread_ts=1791795934.184489)

**Procurement review and supplier implementation.** Public procurement gives a practical customer task: a supplier needs the current requirements, the changes since its earlier review, and a complete source dossier for deciding what to pursue. Our existing [Tonbridge & Malling cemetery opportunity](https://www.sell2wales.gov.wales/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT666186&catID=) identified a secure migration need and a relevant supplier, EDGE IT, whose Epitaph and HeritEDGE products cover cemetery records and mapping. The [original commercial case](https://tokenjunkielabs.slack.com/archives/C0BTTA66TK3/p1791810087835909?thread_ts=1791801709.996379&cid=C0BTTA66TK3) now carries the proposed £7,200 migration-and-mapping workshare, its fifteen-business-day delivery and three milestones, the retained source and the sent first approach. That case supplies a concrete example of the method connecting the source to a complete workshare.

For a funded procurement installation, the buyer would approve one complete review of an agreed procurement process or monitoring period. The merchant would retain the original notices and release editions, produce the comparison and selected review, and deliver the original data, readable report, relational exports and editable receiving workspace together. The buyer would use that result in its existing bid or account workflow. A later amendment, changed period or new source selection provides a distinct useful purchase. The installation work uses the existing Stellar approval, settlement, delivery and recovery components and the application’s six funded packages.

**Coastal model-input commissioning.** Moffatt & Nichol’s published coastal modeling and Digital practices provide a specific prospect for this workflow. The prepared workshare is **USD 18,000 for 150 planned hours over six active working weeks**: one selected study, up to five NOAA stations and five years, one agreed CSV/JSON model-input convention and one deployment environment. The original inquiry was sent on October 12, 2026 to Moffatt & Nichol’s published general-routing mailbox, requesting the coastal, Digital or small-business outreach colleague. The merged Coastal Source Operations product supplies retained source editions, complete study files, explicit mapping and review, returned-file comparison, native query delivery and Python receiving. Commissioning would connect the firm’s actual study, model headings, units, datum and quality decisions to that existing product and finish the installation, refresh procedure and engineer handover. The firm retains model calibration, interpretation and client recommendations. The proposed implementation fee follows USD 5,400 / 7,200 / 5,400 milestones with 15-day terms. A recurring service can supply a newly reviewed station-period release when the source period or edition changes; its useful output is the complete accepted input in the analyst’s existing model. A funded installation would name its commissioning payer, source/release operator, independent buyer and receiving engineer in the original workorder, and price any paid query separately from the implementation work. [Original offer and contact operation](https://tokenjunkielabs.slack.com/archives/C0BTTA66TK3/p1791793139122609) · [Complete commercial and engineering brief](https://tokenjunkielabs.slack.com/docs/T0BRETUB5TK/F0C8GTX1N0J) · [Merged product and operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/92eb1c73a3cab9781ef7dbabdc12067344fb6aa2/products/coops/OPERATING.md).

## Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar is the settlement layer for the approved operation. Buyer approval binds the complete request to its network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount. The native Stellar SDK and configured payment service verify and settle the authorization; the application connects that outcome to the original source, useful result and merchant fulfillment. Buyers control signing and aggregate spending. Merchants control their resources, terms and order actions.

We compose existing ecosystem infrastructure. The x402 Exact Stellar scheme and facilitator supply payment verification and settlement. Vellar’s optional discovery extension publishes eligible settled resources to its catalogue. OpenZeppelin, Veridex and Periplo supply relevant payment infrastructure; Rumble Fish is developing facilitator, discovery and SDK capabilities. Our existing MPP Charge workbench retains that protocol’s own challenge, authorization and recovery model. We use the existing SDK and token contracts.

Our contribution is the repeated source-to-customer operation around those components: preserve the source’s types and pagination; review the exact request and terms; acquire the complete result; receive it into an existing application, report or workbook; and reopen the operating state after interruption or on another authorized host. This gives Stellar merchants a reusable path from a paid endpoint to an independently maintainable customer installation.

A retained comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity. The two-facilitator milestone therefore includes the actual registration and integration work for the same useful service. Its completion will demonstrate that a merchant can change payment infrastructure while preserving the customer operation. Reusable integration, receiving and operating improvements will return to the public source.

## Defined architecture and operating behavior

The system has six components: the merchant’s private source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the native Stellar SDK and selected facilitator; the buyer’s private approval and spending state; complete result and delivery records; and merchant fulfillment/accounting. Node.js supplies the merchant and buyer interfaces. Source adapters and customer applications retain their own native data and operating semantics.

|Stage|Implemented behavior|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Review and publish|The merchant selects a source edition or named live query, request schema, public output, limits and resolved payment options. It reviews rights, route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Later source or terms changes become reviewed states.|
|Connect the source|Adapters preserve types, missing and null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select authorized access. The output identifies its source edition.|
|Approve and purchase|The buyer retains the endpoint, method or MCP tool, arguments, selected terms and scope. The remote schema and challenge must match before signing. Per-payment limits and the application’s existing reservation/budget owner govern spend.|
|Settle and deliver|The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. The application retains the server outcome, complete output and durable merchant notification. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the transaction’s network, asset, parties and atomic amount.|
|Use and continue|The receiving application opens all pages and files required by the agreed task. Its parent acquisition retains the paid requests and incomplete coverage. Earlier acquired output remains available when a later source edition changes.|
|Operate and hand over|The customer selects its release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. A receiving engineer can drain, restart, roll back and restore it with the original operating history and complete customer files.|


For paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments remain distinct from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge. Its full payment option, including authorization timeout, must match the saved quote before the buyer retains dispatch state and sends the signed tool call. The official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata; HTTP operations use the native HTTP transport.

Recovery keeps server confirmation, independently observed transfer, complete output, receiver acknowledgment and fulfillment separately visible. An uncertain signed response retains its original dispatch state for reconciliation. Reopening an acquired result uses the saved work; an unfinished delivery continues from its original intent. A changed request or new purchase receives a new review. Export and restore carry the configuration selection, history and complete referenced files, while the receiving host supplies current authorized secret references.

The same workspaces are available through the browser, terminal, typed clients and MCP. The captured-API product connects reusable route policies to a saved operator procedure, exact native configuration review, continued publication and complete customer files. Its collaboration workflow supports independent draft edits, explicit resolution of overlapping changes and portable working-edit files. The original draft and package writers retain the save, export and receiving lifecycle. This supports installation work by multiple operators while preserving the selected source, procedures and earlier decisions. The buyer accounting product now carries reviewed expense and credit allocations into QuickBooks and Xero using the same connected account. Operators inspect a changed chart, review every affected mapping and journal line, approve the retained plan and recover that original application. Complete source, accountant files and operating history travel with the receiving workspace. [Current buyer workflow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/c0fbc20eb8c8c73c3639c2760f531987e3c6a733/stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/ACCOUNTING_BUYER.md).

## Working product and demonstrated results

Our current network record comprises **18 distinct team-operated development purchases totaling 411,000 stroops, or 0.0411 native testnet XLM**, with fees tracked separately. The retained register connects each purchase to its original transaction and complete output. The funded customer milestones extend this foundation to independently operated services and buyers.

Completed operations show the useful result:

|Operation|Completed result|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Municipal data|A Queens HPD source contained 1,342 building-in-project rows. The selected result received all 144 rows in paid pages of 100 and 44. Both 10,000-stroop transfers finalized, and the full CSV/JSONL edition reopened with source and accounting.|
|Paid agent query|The MariaDB HPD Preservation/minimum-20 query returned all 100 rows, 14 columns and 53,468 bytes for one 50,000-stroop purchase. Scalar strings and its declared truncation indicator were retained. The purchase reopened with signing disconnected; its packet and complete result reopened in another directory. These are project-event records.|
|Filing analysis|A 10,000-stroop purchase delivered the Genpact 2024–2025 comparison: four disclosure pairs, five findings and all 1,027,807 bytes. The editable analyst workspace reopened it, repeat receipt preserved its revision, and backup/restore reproduced the comparison in another installation.|
|Local merchant pricing|The repository fixture’s 1,250-request graduated tariff produced USD 14.25 and a USD 0.0114 uniform quote. The complete original workflow saved and recovered that selection, made the separate asset-price decision, operated both HTTP interfaces, restored the original 110,592-byte pricing backup and reopened the tariff portfolio. The original Merchant Pricing continuation completed all four full exports and retained the combined result. [Completed operation](https://tokenjunkielabs.slack.com/archives/C0BTB4SUCP9/p1791819534159509?thread_ts=1791731109.496529).|


**Complete imagery and processing receiving.** An analyst can open a retained imagery query, browse every scene page, inspect a selected asset, compare source and processing editions, save a reasoned decision, and export the complete GIS and analyst handover. On October 12, the original Node client, CLI and merchant-tool workflow completed all ten native stages using **15 Austin Sentinel-2 scenes across four pages**, the complete **29,731-byte image asset**, and **four Cirrus processing records across two editions**. It exercised full asset streaming and ranges, version-checked review, complete JSON/CSV/HTML reports, imagery and processing import into the receiving workspace, the original cancellation control, and host restart with the same saved operation. Both complete workspaces and their source, decisions, reports and handovers were retained. This receiving operation reused the original captured data; the 18-purchase network baseline remains unchanged. The prospective grant applies these delivered controls to the selected customers’ actual sources, receiving applications, hosts and native Stellar payment terms. [Completed original workflow and operating source](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/2272).

**Prepaid API customer workflow.** A merchant publishes a reviewed allowance plan for a selected application. The customer acquires that plan, sees its available units and each route’s cost, saves an exact request and receives the complete result. Each saved request stays attached to its original pass when the customer changes the default for later work. An exhausted pass can be linked to an explicitly reviewed replacement through the original purchase flow; archived passes keep their earlier results.

The completed funded example bought an eight-unit plan for 10,000 testnet stroops. Its analysis of values 2, 4, 6 and 8 with a two-value window returned all 279 bytes, including count 4, sum 20, mean 5 and window means 2, 3, 5 and 7. That request consumed two units once; reopening it kept six available. Merchant recovery preserved the application result, order, allowance and original settlement outbox. A separate local customer-portfolio operation completed nine customer stages and six authenticated MCP/client/CLI stages, including the original replacement handoff, a resumed response download, five complete exports and cold reopening. This fixture adds no onchain purchase or independent buyer to the network record above.

**Environmental customer operation.** The implemented environmental-data products give this customer task a concrete form. The Laboratory EDD application opens two complete public supplier deliveries with 500 results each, retains original sample/test/batch relationships and reported limits, and lets an operator review current fields, baseline fields and cross-format correspondence separately. Its original native writers reproduce the seven unchanged CSV members. The Water Quality application retains a complete 1,035-result, thirteen-activity cohort and all 1,112 reported limits. Its concentration workflow applies supported reporting units to 298 populated observations and 1,089 limits while preserving all 452 blank-result/unit pairs. For example, 4.65 mg/L silica becomes 4,650 µg/L and its separately reported 0.06 mg/L limit becomes 60 µg/L. The complete source, approved choices and receiving files stay together.

For a commissioned installation, the paid unit is one agreed complete laboratory review/reissue or reporting-window operation. The original buyer approves the function, selected source and review edition, network, asset, recipient and amount. The original merchant runs the computation; the buyer receives the whole archive and opens it in the receiving application. Staff reopen an interrupted request under its original identity. A later source delivery or reporting window becomes a new useful purchase. The implementation work also equips a second operator to receive and maintain that service.

## Threat response and outcome measurement

The day-90 deliverable includes a deployment-specific threat model and an operated monitoring/response plan within the existing 50-hour, USD 4,750 T2 package. Each selected installation records its actual source edition, merchant/buyer authority, network and facilitator, protected evidence, thresholds, notification destinations and named primary/backup responders. Threats are linked to observations and permitted responses: changed offers or approvals, incorrect financial/output attribution, unauthorized authority or access, interrupted delivery, lost monitoring and wrong-generation restore. One confirmed integrity contradiction opens an incident; age, rate and capacity thresholds use reviewed installation values.

Process liveness, native settlement and complete useful output remain separate measures. Missing observations remain a coverage gap, and an uncertain payment reply is reconciled through the original intent rather than authorizing another payment. The two installed response cases are an interrupted settled purchase and a merchant-delivery failure. Acceptance retains the actual notification/acknowledgment, financial and delivery outcomes, response and recovery times, material remediation or residual findings, and the receiving engineer’s same-case reopen after drain/restart. A published design or a local source check does not count as an operated response.

Each merchant’s output must be used by an independent buyer. A completed purchase joins a distinct approved intent, an independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Purchase counts deduplicate native transactions within each network. Buyer counts deduplicate each independent organization or person across its agents and wallets. A returning buyer’s distinct completed purchase increases the purchase count without adding another buyer. Reporting includes completed/attempted purchases, complete/started parent datasets or files, returning buyers, accepted handovers and the cohort’s partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes. Required fulfillment remains separately visible. Reopening an acquired result or resuming its file download continues the original purchase.

For each installation we record the existing customer task and, where available, a prior execution’s active effort, manual corrections and time to useful output. We compare the installed and recurring task against that same input/output definition, retaining the actual source population or period. Customer acceptance and unresolved corrections accompany those measurements. This assesses practical value: usable output, less manual work, repeat demand and a service the customer’s engineer can maintain.

Node.js supplies the merchant and buyer interfaces. Source adapters and customer applications retain their own native data and operating semantics.

|Stage|Implemented behavior|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Review and publish|The merchant selects a source edition or named live query, request schema, public output, limits and resolved payment options. It reviews rights, route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Later source or terms changes become reviewed states.|
|Connect the source|Adapters preserve types, missing and null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select authorized access. The output identifies its source edition.|
|Approve and purchase|The buyer retains the endpoint, method or MCP tool, arguments, selected terms and scope. The remote schema and challenge must match before signing. Per-payment limits and the application’s existing reservation/budget owner govern spend.|
|Settle and deliver|The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. The application retains the server outcome, complete output and durable merchant notification. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the transaction’s network, asset, parties and atomic amount.|
|Use and continue|The receiving application opens all pages and files required by the agreed task. Its parent acquisition retains the paid requests and incomplete coverage. Earlier acquired output remains available when a later source edition changes.|
|Operate and hand over|The customer selects its release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. A receiving engineer can drain, restart, roll back and restore it with the original operating history and complete customer files.|


For paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments remain distinct from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge. Its full payment option, including authorization timeout, must match the saved quote before the buyer retains dispatch state and sends the signed tool call. The official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata; HTTP operations use the native HTTP transport.

Recovery keeps server confirmation, independently observed transfer, complete output, receiver acknowledgment and fulfillment separately visible. An uncertain signed response retains its original dispatch state for reconciliation. Reopening an acquired result uses the saved work; an unfinished delivery continues from its original intent. A changed request or new purchase receives a new review. Export and restore carry the configuration selection, history and complete referenced files, while the receiving host supplies current authorized secret references.

The same workspaces are available through the browser, terminal, typed clients and MCP. The captured-API product connects reusable route policies to a saved operator procedure, exact native configuration review, continued publication and complete customer files. Its collaboration workflow supports independent draft edits, explicit resolution of overlapping changes and portable working-edit files. The original draft and package writers retain the save, export and receiving lifecycle. This supports installation work by multiple operators while preserving the selected source, procedures and earlier decisions. The buyer accounting product now carries reviewed expense and credit allocations into QuickBooks and Xero using the same connected account. Operators inspect a changed chart, review every affected mapping and journal line, approve the retained plan and recover that original application. Complete source, accountant files and operating history travel with the receiving workspace. The retained register connects each purchase to its original transaction and complete output. The funded customer milestones extend this foundation to independently operated services and buyers.

Completed operations show the useful result:

|Operation|Completed result|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Municipal data|A Queens HPD source contained 1,342 building-in-project rows. The selected result received all 144 rows in paid pages of 100 and 44. Both 10,000-stroop transfers finalized, and the full CSV/JSONL edition reopened with source and accounting.|
|Paid agent query|The MariaDB HPD Preservation/minimum-20 query returned all 100 rows, 14 columns and 53,468 bytes for one 50,000-stroop purchase. Scalar strings and its declared truncation indicator were retained. The purchase reopened with signing disconnected; its packet and complete result reopened in another directory. These are project-event records.|
|Filing analysis|A 10,000-stroop purchase delivered the Genpact 2024–2025 comparison: four disclosure pairs, five findings and all 1,027,807 bytes. The editable analyst workspace reopened it, repeat receipt preserved its revision, and backup/restore reproduced the comparison in another installation.|
|Local merchant pricing|The repository fixture’s 1,250-request graduated tariff produced USD 14.25 and a USD 0.0114 uniform quote. The complete original workflow saved and recovered that selection, made the separate asset-price decision, operated both HTTP interfaces, restored the original 110,592-byte pricing backup and reopened the tariff portfolio. The original Merchant Pricing continuation completed all four full exports and retained the combined result. [Completed operation](https://tokenjunkielabs.slack.com/archives/C0BTB4SUCP9/p1791819534159509?thread_ts=1791731109.496529).|


**Complete imagery and processing receiving.** An analyst can open a retained imagery query, browse every scene page, inspect a selected asset, compare source and processing editions, save a reasoned decision, and export the complete GIS and analyst handover. On October 12, the original Node client, CLI and merchant-tool workflow completed all ten native stages using **15 Austin Sentinel-2 scenes across four pages**, the complete **29,731-byte image asset**, and **four Cirrus processing records across two editions**. It exercised full asset streaming and ranges, version-checked review, complete JSON/CSV/HTML reports, imagery and processing import into the receiving workspace, the original cancellation control, and host restart with the same saved operation. Both complete workspaces and their source, decisions, reports and handovers were retained. This receiving operation reused the original captured data; the 18-purchase network baseline remains unchanged. The prospective grant applies these delivered controls to the selected customers’ actual sources, receiving applications, hosts and native Stellar payment terms. [Completed original workflow and operating source](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/2272).

**Prepaid API customer workflow.** A merchant publishes a reviewed allowance plan for a selected application. The customer acquires that plan, sees its available units and each route’s cost, saves an exact request and receives the complete result. Each saved request stays attached to its original pass when the customer changes the default for later work. An exhausted pass can be linked to an explicitly reviewed replacement through the original purchase flow; archived passes keep their earlier results.

The completed funded example bought an eight-unit plan for 10,000 testnet stroops. Its analysis of values 2, 4, 6 and 8 with a two-value window returned all 279 bytes, including count 4, sum 20, mean 5 and window means 2, 3, 5 and 7. That request consumed two units once; reopening it kept six available. Merchant recovery preserved the application result, order, allowance and original settlement outbox. A separate local customer-portfolio operation completed nine customer stages and six authenticated MCP/client/CLI stages, including the original replacement handoff, a resumed response download, five complete exports and cold reopening. This fixture adds no onchain purchase or independent buyer to the network record above.

**Environmental customer operation.** The implemented environmental-data products give this customer task a concrete form. The Laboratory EDD application opens two complete public supplier deliveries with 500 results each, retains original sample/test/batch relationships and reported limits, and lets an operator review current fields, baseline fields and cross-format correspondence separately. Its original native writers reproduce the seven unchanged CSV members. The Water Quality application retains a complete 1,035-result, thirteen-activity cohort and all 1,112 reported limits. Its concentration workflow applies supported reporting units to 298 populated observations and 1,089 limits while preserving all 452 blank-result/unit pairs. For example, 4.65 mg/L silica becomes 4,650 µg/L and its separately reported 0.06 mg/L limit becomes 60 µg/L. The complete source, approved choices and receiving files stay together.

For a commissioned installation, the paid unit is one agreed complete laboratory review/reissue or reporting-window operation. The original buyer approves the function, selected source and review edition, network, asset, recipient and amount. The original merchant runs the computation; the buyer receives the whole archive and opens it in the receiving application. Staff reopen an interrupted request under its original identity. A later source delivery or reporting window becomes a new useful purchase. The implementation work also equips a second operator to receive and maintain that service.

**Federal-award research and workshares.** The merged federal-awards product follows an original award edition through complete transaction history, chronological funding changes, an editable proposed workshare and a portable customer dossier. Browser, terminal, native merchant tools and managed Applications use the same private research workspace. The analyst retains the agency roles, exact source amounts and original action descriptions while saving the proposed delivery, acceptance and relationship owner against that source. A receiving engineer can reopen the original record and continue its research.

The retained official example is Carahsoft delivery order **47QACA26F0383**, for agentic artificial intelligence implementation: GSA’s Federal Acquisition Service is the awarding agency and OPM is the funding agency. Its two transaction obligations are **$1,666,999.96** and **$437,800.00**, totaling **$2,104,799.96**. The latter keeps its original **OTHER ADMINISTRATIVE ACTION** description alongside the positive funding amount. The application also retains the separately reported **$8,772,799.80** all-options value. This makes the research usable without collapsing different contract values or the source’s action classification.

For a commissioned installation, the useful recurring task is an agreed award-data edition or complete funding-change research delivery. T1 connects that selected output, public projection and customer receiving application to the existing Stellar merchant and buyer flow. A later source observation gives the buyer a distinct update to review and purchase. The complete [maintained installation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/tree/87801e395d496ffb36fba5cd7215ea942ed96aa2/products/federal-awards), operating sequence and six-package linkage are included in §9A.

The identified agent-query example completed on October 11 at 20:12:58 UTC, Stellar testnet ledger **5,145,195**, transaction **50d61d1102bfcf960af44171e5248e0899ed6d99cec1951a62075f9a65a6cbed**. Its full result SHA-256 is **4c22f8a26d48156c3e07543328b62ca6f993ce60856166d6805dc0660d9acb8d**. This identifies the operated result underlying the product demonstration.

Complete receiving has also preserved all sixteen rows of a Census workbook across CSV, JSONL, SQLite, browser and Rust clients; a later edition identified fifteen unchanged rows and one changed row while the earlier customer retained its original values. The supplier workflow imported both complete 106-material SAP SHINE publisher editions, reviewed their supplier changes and reopened the full catalogue handover. An installed incident-to-case operation completed an observation gap, notification retry, acknowledgment, recovery and support-case reopening.

**Recurring economic reports.** The economic briefing application turns a reviewed selection of unemployment, prices and GDP observations into a reusable reporting procedure. An analyst keeps the selected series, period comparisons, units, missing-value treatment and calendar policy, then previews the next report against a retained source edition. The comparison shows new periods, periods leaving the window and revisions to values or baselines. Each saved successor retains its original capture, analyst review and complete report; the preceding edition stays available.

For a commissioned installation, the merchant is the organization publishing the reviewed report, the buyer is the independent analyst or application using it, and the commissioning payer funds the agreed implementation. Those roles and the receiving maintainer are named in the original workorder. One useful priced operation is a complete advertised `briefing.html` or `briefing.json` download. It contains the selected measurements and the source observations used by their calculations. The buyer reviews that exact GET resource, network, asset, recipient, atomic amount and expected file before the original Stellar payment path delivers it. Opening the retained result continues the original purchase. A later reporting window or revised source edition supplies the reason for a distinct purchase.

The existing [recurring briefing product and operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/be44be564e35b63af23246bad531a95374bbb4c0/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/fred/TEMPLATES.md) supplies the analyst workflow, private browser, CLI, typed client, merchant tools and complete project receiving. The funded work adapts that product to the selected customer’s source, report, native terms, hosts and receiving application, then completes the common independent-use and handover milestones.

The captioned **3-minute-32-second product/team film** follows the native HPD query, saved terms, one 0.005-testnet-XLM purchase, complete result, download and reopening. Its editable companion includes eleven clips, captions, script, result and rendering tools. The reviewer workbench has completed original-packet receiving, full-result reads, export, cold reopening and second-operator receiving across desktop and 390-pixel mobile views. The delivered Customers workspace extends that review through the merchant host: configured packet intake, complete saved results, original source documents, closed export and full receiving files. Its saved fourteen-step delivery and six-step receiving workflows keep the original operations together. Each selected installation records its actual source edition, merchant/buyer authority, network and facilitator, protected evidence, thresholds, notification destinations and named primary/backup responders. Threats are linked to observations and permitted responses: changed offers or approvals, incorrect financial/output attribution, unauthorized authority or access, interrupted delivery, lost monitoring and wrong-generation restore. One confirmed integrity contradiction opens an incident; age, rate and capacity thresholds use reviewed installation values.

Process liveness, native settlement and complete useful output remain separate measures. Missing observations remain a coverage gap, and an uncertain payment reply is reconciled through the original intent rather than authorizing another payment. The two installed response cases are an interrupted settled purchase and a merchant-delivery failure. Acceptance retains the actual notification/acknowledgment, financial and delivery outcomes, response and recovery times, material remediation or residual findings, and the receiving engineer’s same-case reopen after drain/restart. A published design or a local source check does not count as an operated response.

Each merchant’s output must be used by an independent buyer. A completed purchase joins a distinct approved intent, an independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Purchase counts deduplicate native transactions within each network. Buyer counts deduplicate each independent organization or person across its agents and wallets. A returning buyer’s distinct completed purchase increases the purchase count without adding another buyer. Reporting includes completed/attempted purchases, complete/started parent datasets or files, returning buyers, accepted handovers and the cohort’s partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes. Required fulfillment remains separately visible. Reopening an acquired result or resuming its file download continues the original purchase.

For each installation we record the existing customer task and, where available, a prior execution’s active effort, manual corrections and time to useful output. We compare the installed and recurring task against that same input/output definition, retaining the actual source population or period. Customer acceptance and unresolved corrections accompany those measurements. Merchants retain their resource receipts, while TokenJunkieLabs invoices its agreed engineering and handover. A merchant selects the resource and commercial terms; a buyer approves a specific request and controls its wallet and spending. The software carries that agreement through native settlement, complete usable output, fulfillment, recovery and handover to another engineer.\\n\\nWe request **USD 38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance**. The award will fund the remaining source, consumer and deployment engineering for **two independently operated merchants and two independent buyer operators**, including completion of the same useful operation through **two independently operated facilitators**. The delivered result will be a maintainable service on Stellar mainnet, with recurring customer use and an independently completed recovery and handover.\\n\\nThe existing product supplies the architecture, merchant and buyer workspaces, source adapters, payment integration, result receiving and operating controls. The six funded packages below apply that product to the selected customers’ actual sources, applications and hosts. They include installation-specific implementation and defects, provider integration, deployed threat response, production release and technical receiving.\\n\\n## Customer problem, need and adoption\\n\\nAPI and data operators want to sell useful operations to applications and agents while retaining source rights, access rules and commercial control. Buyers need the complete result they approved, in a form their existing application can use. Buyer approval binds the complete request to its network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount. Reviewer application\\n\\n**Stellar Discovery Trust Layer — TokenJunkieLabs — SCF #46 Build / Open Track**\\n\\n## Project and requested outcome\\n\\nWe are building open-source, self-hostable software for operating paid APIs, datasets and agent tools on Stellar. A merchant selects the resource and commercial terms; a buyer approves a specific request and controls its wallet and spending. The software carries that agreement through native settlement, complete usable output, fulfillment, recovery and handover to another engineer.\\n\\nWe request **USD 38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance**. The award will fund the remaining source, consumer and deployment engineering for **two independently operated merchants and two independent buyer operators**, including completion of the same useful operation through **two independently operated facilitators**. The delivered result will be a maintainable service on Stellar mainnet, with recurring customer use and an independently completed recovery and handover.\\n\\nThe existing product supplies the architecture, merchant and buyer workspaces, source adapters, payment integration, result receiving and operating controls. The six funded packages below apply that product to the selected customers’ actual sources, applications and hosts. They include installation-specific implementation and defects, provider integration, deployed threat response, production release and technical receiving.\\n\\n## Customer problem, need and adoption\\n\\nAPI and data operators want to sell useful operations to applications and agents while retaining source rights, access rules and commercial control. Buyers need the complete result they approved, in a form their existing application can use. Staff also need to recover an interrupted paid request and transfer the working service to another maintainer.\\n\\nThat task joins four records: the approved request, the settled transfer, the delivered output and the accepted fulfillment or accounting. A payment confirmation alone does not show whether a multi-page dataset is complete, whether its values retained their original meaning, or whether an order reached its intended state. The customer’s useful task can contain several priced requests, so its aggregate cost and complete output must remain visible.\\n\\nPublic October 2–3 x402 reports illustrate this operational need: one merchant rejected payment-bearing requests because its POST requirement differed from a client’s GET retry; another reported settlement without its expected discovery listing. These reports concerned Base deployments, and their follow-ups include a corrected server and successful indexing. They inform the request, discovery and recovery joins we implement on Stellar.\\n\\nOur current human conversations provide more specific customer learning:\\n\\n|Organization|Observed response|Proposed useful implementation|\\n|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |\\n|Veridex|Invited an open testnet design partnership after declining a third-party testing budget.|One agreed testnet route and buyer adaptation, proposed at $1,500 over five business days.|\\n|Nansen|Referred the proposal internally and confirmed on October 12 that the Holdings detail was included.|Read-only Ethereum Holdings data, Stellar testnet payment and source/operator handover, proposed at $2,400 over five business days.|\\n|CoCart|Founder Sébastien Dumont asked about introductions, the payer, referral compensation, responsibilities and contracting.|One customer’s headless cart, native WooCommerce checkout, payment/order operation and receiving, proposed at $7,200 for 60 hours over fifteen business days.|\\n|Blockscout|Mojmir Racak expressed interest on October 12 and reported no current integration budget.|One approved PRO API token-information operation, buyer integration and handover, proposed at $4,800 over ten business days.|\\n\\n\\nThese conversations identify the practical selection decisions: a recurring buyer task, usable source rights, an accountable merchant host, an independent receiving application and an agreed commissioning payer. A participating platform and the organization paying for its integration can be different organizations. For CoCart, the first merchant or agency and commissioning arrangement remain to be selected. Bryce owns these favorable relationships and subsequent agreements.\\n\\nFor each funded installation, the original workorder will name the payer, merchant, buyer and receiving operator; the source and authorized access; the exact request, complete output and priced unit; the host and receiving application; and the person accepting delivery. It will record what makes a later purchase useful, such as a fresh period, changed source edition or new customer request. The implementation team then takes that same task through deployment, complete result receiving, recurring use and maintainer handover.\\n\\n**Environmental provider intake supplies a concrete commissioning path.** Axiom Data Science's [published sensor-intake guidance](https://www.axiomdatascience.com/best-practices/SubmitDataSensors.html) describes delays caused by inconsistent provider fields and asks for station, time, quality, contact and licensing context. Our proposed workshare applies the complete ERDDAP provider workspace to three agreed feeds, one client-managed Linux installation and one file/command receiving integration: **$12,600 / 96 hours / 18 active business days**, including eight support hours during the first 30 days after acceptance. The first contact and four customer documents were sent on October 12; commissioning remains open. The original public-source operation has received a complete 144-row NDBC dataset and saved three provider-review revisions, with earlier exports preserved through an evaluator upgrade. Its selected installation and browser continuation remain pending. If selected for funded deployment, the parties would agree the merchant, independent buyer, exact useful output and payment terms in the original workorder. §9A connects this task to the existing six funded packages. [Current product and operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/5f7143f88bb28fbd0c1b63a913545633c475afd6/products/erddap-provider/OPERATING.md) · [Original commercial delivery](https://tokenjunkielabs.slack.com/archives/C0BTTA66TK3/p1791809627823129?thread_ts=1791795934.184489)\\n\\n**Procurement review and supplier implementation.** Public procurement gives a practical customer task: a supplier needs the current requirements, the changes since its earlier review, and a complete source dossier for deciding what to pursue. Our existing [Tonbridge & Malling cemetery opportunity](https://www.sell2wales.gov.wales/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT666186&catID=) identified a secure migration need and a relevant supplier, EDGE IT, whose Epitaph and HeritEDGE products cover cemetery records and mapping. The [original commercial case](https://tokenjunkielabs.slack.com/archives/C0BTTA66TK3/p1791810087835909?thread_ts=1791801709.996379&cid=C0BTTA66TK3) now carries the proposed £7,200 migration-and-mapping workshare, its fifteen-business-day delivery and three milestones, the retained source and the sent first approach. That case supplies a concrete example of the method connecting the source to a complete workshare.\\n\\nFor a funded procurement installation, the buyer would approve one complete review of an agreed procurement process or monitoring period. The merchant would retain the original notices and release editions, produce the comparison and selected review, and deliver the original data, readable report, relational exports and editable receiving workspace together. The buyer would use that result in its existing bid or account workflow. A later amendment, changed period or new source selection provides a distinct useful purchase. The installation work uses the existing Stellar approval, settlement, delivery and recovery components and the application’s six funded packages.\\n\\n**Coastal model-input commissioning.** Moffatt & Nichol’s published coastal modeling and Digital practices provide a specific prospect for this workflow. The prepared workshare is **USD 18,000 for 150 planned hours over six active working weeks**: one selected study, up to five NOAA stations and five years, one agreed CSV/JSON model-input convention and one deployment environment. The original inquiry was sent on October 12, 2026 to Moffatt & Nichol’s published general-routing mailbox, requesting the coastal, Digital or small-business outreach colleague. The merged Coastal Source Operations product supplies retained source editions, complete study files, explicit mapping and review, returned-file comparison, native query delivery and Python receiving. Commissioning would connect the firm’s actual study, model headings, units, datum and quality decisions to that existing product and finish the installation, refresh procedure and engineer handover. The firm retains model calibration, interpretation and client recommendations. The proposed implementation fee follows USD 5,400 / 7,200 / 5,400 milestones with 15-day terms. A recurring service can supply a newly reviewed station-period release when the source period or edition changes; its useful output is the complete accepted input in the analyst’s existing model. A funded installation would name its commissioning payer, source/release operator, independent buyer and receiving engineer in the original workorder, and price any paid query separately from the implementation work. [Original offer and contact operation](https://tokenjunkielabs.slack.com/archives/C0BTTA66TK3/p1791793139122609) · [Complete commercial and engineering brief](https://tokenjunkielabs.slack.com/docs/T0BRETUB5TK/F0C8GTX1N0J) · [Merged product and operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/92eb1c73a3cab9781ef7dbabdc12067344fb6aa2/products/coops/OPERATING.md).\\n\\n## Why Stellar and what we contribute\\n\\nStellar is the settlement layer for the approved operation. Buyer approval binds the complete request to its network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount. The native Stellar SDK and configured payment service verify and settle the authorization; the application connects that outcome to the original source, useful result and merchant fulfillment. Buyers control signing and aggregate spending. Merchants control their resources, terms and order actions.\\n\\nWe compose existing ecosystem infrastructure. The x402 Exact Stellar scheme and facilitator supply payment verification and settlement. Vellar’s optional discovery extension publishes eligible settled resources to its catalogue. OpenZeppelin, Veridex and Periplo supply relevant payment infrastructure; Rumble Fish is developing facilitator, discovery and SDK capabilities. Our existing MPP Charge workbench retains that protocol’s own challenge, authorization and recovery model. We use the existing SDK and token contracts.\\n\\nOur contribution is the repeated source-to-customer operation around those components: preserve the source’s types and pagination; review the exact request and terms; acquire the complete result; receive it into an existing application, report or workbook; and reopen the operating state after interruption or on another authorized host. This gives Stellar merchants a reusable path from a paid endpoint to an independently maintainable customer installation.\\n\\nA retained comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity. The two-facilitator milestone therefore includes the actual registration and integration work for the same useful service. Its completion will demonstrate that a merchant can change payment infrastructure while preserving the customer operation. Reusable integration, receiving and operating improvements will return to the public source.\\n\\n## Defined architecture and operating behavior\\n\\nThe system has six components: the merchant’s private source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the native Stellar SDK and selected facilitator; the buyer’s private approval and spending state; complete result and delivery records; and merchant fulfillment/accounting. Node.js supplies the merchant and buyer interfaces. Source adapters and customer applications retain their own native data and operating semantics.\\n\\n|Stage|Implemented behavior|\\n|  ---  |  ---  |\\n|Review and publish|The merchant selects a source edition or named live query, request schema, public output, limits and resolved payment options. It reviews rights, route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Later source or terms changes become reviewed states.|\\n|Connect the source|Adapters preserve types, missing and null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select authorized access. The output identifies its source edition.|\\n|Approve and purchase|The buyer retains the endpoint, method or MCP tool, arguments, selected terms and scope. The remote schema and challenge must match before signing. Per-payment limits and the application’s existing reservation/budget owner govern spend.|\\n|Settle and deliver|The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. The application retains the server outcome, complete output and durable merchant notification. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the transaction’s network, asset, parties and atomic amount.|\\n|Use and continue|The receiving application opens all pages and files required by the agreed task. Its parent acquisition retains the paid requests and incomplete coverage. Earlier acquired output remains available when a later source edition changes.|\\n|Operate and hand over|The customer selects its release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. A receiving engineer can drain, restart, roll back and restore it with the original operating history and complete customer files.|\\n\\n\\nFor paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments remain distinct from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge. Its full payment option, including authorization timeout, must match the saved quote before the buyer retains dispatch state and sends the signed tool call. The official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata; HTTP operations use the native HTTP transport.\\n\\nRecovery keeps server confirmation, independently observed transfer, complete output, receiver acknowledgment and fulfillment separately visible. An uncertain signed response retains its original dispatch state for reconciliation. Reopening an acquired result uses the saved work; an unfinished delivery continues from its original intent. A changed request or new purchase receives a new review. Export and restore carry the configuration selection, history and complete referenced files, while the receiving host supplies current authorized secret references.\\n\\nThe same workspaces are available through the browser, terminal, typed clients and MCP. The captured-API product connects reusable route policies to a saved operator procedure, exact native configuration review, continued publication and complete customer files. Its collaboration workflow supports independent draft edits, explicit resolution of overlapping changes and portable working-edit files. The original draft and package writers retain the save, export and receiving lifecycle. This supports installation work by multiple operators while preserving the selected source, procedures and earlier decisions. The buyer accounting product now carries reviewed expense and credit allocations into QuickBooks and Xero using the same connected account. Operators inspect a changed chart, review every affected mapping and journal line, approve the retained plan and recover that original application. Complete source, accountant files and operating history travel with the receiving workspace. A separate local customer-portfolio operation completed nine customer stages and six authenticated MCP/client/CLI stages, including the original replacement handoff, a resumed response download, five complete exports and cold reopening. The Laboratory EDD application opens two complete public supplier deliveries with 500 results each, retains original sample/test/batch relationships and reported limits, and lets an operator review current fields, baseline fields and cross-format correspondence separately. Its original native writers reproduce the seven unchanged CSV members. The Water Quality application retains a complete 1,035-result, thirteen-activity cohort and all 1,112 reported limits. Its concentration workflow applies supported reporting units to 298 populated observations and 1,089 limits while preserving all 452 blank-result/unit pairs. For example, 4.65 mg/L silica becomes 4,650 µg/L and its separately reported 0.06 mg/L limit becomes 60 µg/L. The complete source, approved choices and receiving files stay together.\\n\\nFor a commissioned installation, the paid unit is one agreed complete laboratory review/reissue or reporting-window operation. The original buyer approves the function, selected source and review edition, network, asset, recipient and amount. The original merchant runs the computation; the buyer receives the whole archive and opens it in the receiving application. Staff reopen an interrupted request under its original identity. A later source delivery or reporting window becomes a new useful purchase. Earlier acquired output remains available when a later source edition changes.|\\n|Operate and hand over|The customer selects its release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. A receiving engineer can drain, restart, roll back and restore it with the original operating history and complete customer files.|\\n\\n\\nFor paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments remain distinct from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge. Its full payment option, including authorization timeout, must match the saved quote before the buyer retains dispatch state and sends the signed tool call.
